title: Attempt on No infinite cluster at criticality on quasi-transitive graphs with p_c < 1
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Split by growth type and identify the remaining cases precisely. Result: By Trofimov's theorem a quasi-transitive graph of polynomial growth is quasi-isometric to a Cayley graph of a virtually nilpotent group, and the critical behaviour of percolation is not a quasi-isometry invariant in general, so this does not reduce directly to Z^d; however the known proof for Z^2 (Harris-Kesten) and the high-dimensional proof (lace expansion, d >= 11) do not transfer either. Exponential growth is Hutchcroft's theorem. The remaining cases are (a) polynomial growth of degree 3 to 10 (and all virtually nilpotent non-abelian cases, e.g. the Heisenberg group of growth degree 4), where the problem is at least as hard as C0023, and (b) intermediate growth (Grigorchuk-type groups), where Hutchcroft's argument fails because it uses that the number of vertices at distance n grows exponentially to compare the cluster with a branching structure. For case (b) I checked the two known routes: the nonamenable route (Burton-Keane fails, so uniqueness monotonicity gives theta(p_c)=0 through the Benjamini-Lyons-Peres-Schramm argument) does not apply since intermediate-growth groups are amenable; the exponential-growth route uses a subadditivity argument on the expected number of vertices at distance n reached by the cluster, which requires growth rate > 1 in the exponential sense. Intermediate growth groups have growth exp(n^alpha), alpha < 1, which is superpolynomial, and Hutchcroft's argument actually needs only that the growth is faster than any polynomial? His proof uses the growth to show that the susceptibility is finite at p_c in a spherically-averaged sense via a comparison with a branching random walk with killing at rate given by the growth; I believe the argument requires exponential growth for the comparison to be uniform, so intermediate growth is a genuine gap. Recorded: the open cases are polynomial growth (degree 3 to 10 and non-abelian nilpotent) and intermediate growth. Obstruction: Polynomial growth is the Z^d problem; intermediate growth defeats the exponential-growth comparison.

title: Open problem: Absence of infinite clusters at critical percolation
body:
OPEN PROBLEM from the Codex campaign ledger (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). If G is quasi-transitive and p_c(G)<1, is there almost surely no infinite Bernoulli cluster at p_c(G)? Source: Probability on Trees and Networks, paperback electronic version 19 August 2026, Conjecture 8.15, printed p.285.
Posed in Probability on Trees and Networks, paperback electronic version 19 August 2026
